 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 13.11.2020.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 13.11.2020 at about 05.20pm while the petitioner was standing infront of KIA Showroom near Mysore Road, Kengeri, Bangalore, a KIA Car T/R No.KA2020-T-R-8951BG, SCCH - 25 3 MVC No.4514/2020 ENG.No.D4FALM054829, CHASSIS No.MZBEP813LLN49558 driven by its driver with a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to this terrific act petitioner fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to BGS Global Hospital, Bangalore.
For further treatment he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore, underwent treatment and discharged with an advice to take complete rest.
So far he has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medicines.
At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, working in KIA Showroom as Salesman and earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he became disabled and could not work as before the accident.
He lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the C a r b e a r i n g N o . K A 2 0 2 0 - T - R - 8 9 5 1 B G , E N G . N o .
D 4 F A L M 0 5 4 8 2 9 , C H A S S I S No.MZBEP813LLN49558.
The Kengeri Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.93/2020.

Therefore, the SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.4514/2020 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
3. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear and was placed exparte.
4. The objection of the respondent No.2.
It has denied all the averments made in the petition.
The petition is also bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
Further denied the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car T/R No.KA2020-T-R-8951BG, ENG.No.D4FALM054829, CHASSIS No.MZBEP813LLN49558.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner who without observing movement of the vehicle suddenly rushed, which resulted in alleged accident.
As on the date of accident the SCCH - 25 5 MVC No.4514/2020 driver of the the Car T/R No.KA2020-T-R-8951BG, ENG.No.D4FALM054829, CHASSIS No.MZBEP813LLN49558 Rakshith.

sentences.text: It has denied the accidental injuries of the petitioner.

5. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 13.11.2020 at about 5.20pm, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the the Car T/R N o . K A 2 0 2 0 - T - R - 8 9 5 1 B G , E N G . N o . D 4 F A L M 0 5 4 8 2 9 , C H A S S I S No.MZBEP813LLN49558 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries.?
2.
Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
He has also got examined Smt. Shanthamma - Medical Record SCCH - 25 6 MVC No.4514/2020 Officer as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 to P.18.
Dr.Chetan A got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.19 & 20.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
8.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the the Car T/R No.KA2020-T-R-8951BG, ENG.No.D4FALM054829, CHASSIS No.MZBEP813LLN49558, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.7.
He SCCH - 25 7 MVC No.4514/2020 has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated that the offending Car was prepared for delivery in the showroom and it was in the delivery area.
He was standing 70-80mt away from it.
He has also got examined the MRO as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 to P.18 Authorization letter, MLC register extract, police intimation, out patient record and inpatient files 3 in Nos.
During her cross examination, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent No.2 insurer has contended that there was sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
In order to prove its contention it has not examined any witness.

sentences.text: The FIR at Ex.P.1, was registered on the next day of the accident i.e., on 14.11.2020 on the complaint at Ex.P.2 given by the Father of the petitioner.
Spot Mahazar and spot sketch and statement of witnesses at Exs.P.3, 4 & 6 are all in accordance with the statement given by the Father of the petitioner.
Ex.P.5 is the notice given to the owner of the offending vehicle and reply.

The police have conducted SCCH - 25 8 MVC No.4514/2020 investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 against the driver of the Car T/R No.KA2020-T-R-8951BG, ENG.No.D4FALM054829,
CHASSIS No.MZBEP813LLN49558.
Therefore, on perusal of the above said documents produced by the petitioner, they show that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the Petitioner has suffered (i) Left both bone fracture and right open both bone fracture leg which are grievous in nature.
12. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Chetan A. as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.19 & 20 OPD Card and X-ray film with report.

He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed to have fracture both bones of left leg distal third and fracture both bones of SCCH - 25 9 MVC No.4514/2020 right leg distal third.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from permanent partial impairment of both lower limbs at 54% and to the whole body at 18%.
13. PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that he has treated the petitioner and conducted the surgery.
The petitioner has suffered fracture of both legs but surgery was done on both tibia.
Fractures are united.
Implants are removed.

Disability:
14.
From the evidence of PW.3 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered fractures of both bones of both leg.
Further stated that petitioner is said to be a Salesman and with the said disabilities, he cannot carryout his activities like walking and standing long time.
This means that he has to sit and do the work.
PW.3 has also stated that the petitioner can do desk job.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 15%.

SCCH - 25 10 MVC No.4514/2020  Monthly income:
15.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Salesman and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.14,500/- per month.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at BGS Global Hospital, provided firstaid and thereafter he was shifted to HOSMAT Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 13.11.2020 to 18.11.2020 and again admitted from 19.11.2020 to 01.12.2023 and again he was admitted for removal of implants on 24.01.2024 to SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.4514/2020 26.01.2024, diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.10.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.2,52,438/-.
Out of these bills, Sl.No.5 bill paid by the Royal Sundaram for Rs.708/- which has to be deducted in total amount.
As such, after deduction a sum of Rs.2,51,730/- is the medical expenses.
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of SCCH - 25 12 MVC No.4514/2020 HOSMAT Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.

Hence,
he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.29,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.13, the petitioner's age is mentioned as 27 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 27 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,43,700/- (Rs.14,500/- x 12 x 17 x 15%= Rs.4,43,700/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-

sentences.text: The Petitioner was aged about 27 years at the time of accident.

He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 15%
SCCH - 25 13 MVC No.4514/2020 functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

16. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,51,730/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.29,000/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.4,43,700/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 SCCH - 25 14 MVC No.4514/2020  happiness  6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
 nourishment charges
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.8,44,500/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Liability 17.
The Respondents have contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

sentences.text: However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.51,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.8,44,500/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.4514/2020 Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,44,500/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Forty Four Thousand and Five Hundred only)
along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.4514/2020 with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any Bank of his choice and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e- payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules

. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
